text:
Harpreet S.: Quick announcement: starting July 1 we’re rolling out a 2-day Volunteer Leave pilot (VLP) so folks can take paid time to volunteer with registered non-profits. Details + how to sign up: https://intranet.redwood.com/policies/volunteer-leave

Darren M.: Awesome. Is this separate from VTO or is it replacing something?

People Ops: Short answer: separate pilot. VTO remains (informal ad-hoc time) but VLP is formal paid leave tied to registered organizations and includes an approval flow and reporting for program partners.

Sam L.: Who approves the leave? manager or People Ops?

People Ops: Manager approval required to confirm coverage. People Ops verifies the nonprofit status post-approval (we only accept registrations from recognized charities). Aim: <3 business day turnaround.

Harpreet S.: Any restrictions on how to use the 2 days? partial days ok?

People Ops: Partial days allowed (min 4 hours). You can take the 2 days in one block or separately. Cannot be used concurrently with other company leaves for the same hours.

Darren M.: Will this affect payroll or PTO balances?

People Ops: It’s a separate paid leave bucket and does not deduct from your PTO. Payroll unaffected.

Sam L.: Are contractors eligible?

People Ops: Not in pilot. We’re starting with full-time and part-time employees. We’ll evaluate contractor inclusion after the pilot.

Harpreet S.: Any reporting required by employees after volunteering?

People Ops: Yes  quick confirmation form in Workday (non-sensitive): organization name, date, hours, and a short attestation. We do a random sample verification with partners to prevent abuse.

Legal Bot: :information_source: Note from Legal: do not present VLP as insurance or endorsement of any third party. If the volunteer role involves travel or working with minors, submit the extra waiver at least 10 days before activity. See legal guidance: https://intranet.redwood.com/legal/volunteer-guidance

Darren M.: Speaking of travel, any code-of-conduct reminders for people speaking at conferences on company travel?

People Ops: Good point  we updated the Travel & External Events code-of-conduct. If you represent Redwood externally you must complete the External Presenter Acknowledgement in Concur 7 days before travel. It includes media guidelines and harassment expectations.

Sam L.: What happens if someone violates the conduct rules while at an event?

People Ops: Violations are handled per our standard conduct process. Immediate safety concerns: contact Security and People Ops. For other cases, People Ops & Legal will investigate; outcomes may include revocation of travel privileges.

Harpreet S.: Can we get a 1-paragraph blurb for team leads to share?

People Ops: Yes  posting a TL;DR and email template in #announcements now, plus a manager one-pager in #managers. Also dropping a short slide deck for all-hands next week.

Sam L.: Is the pilot timeboxed?

People Ops: Pilot runs July 1 through Dec 31. We’ll share mid-pilot usage in Sep and a final review in Jan. If successful, we’ll propose making it permanent.

Darren M.: Any tax or compliance notes for international employees?

People Ops: Some countries treat employer-sponsored leave differently. Check the per-country note on the policy page. People Ops will reach out to local leads if there are restrictions.

Harpreet S.: Thanks all. If anyone has partner suggestions for community orgs, DM me. :heart:

People Ops: Ping people-ops@redwood.com for questions or edge cases. Thanks!
